newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Man shot dead in U.S. visa riot in Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Man shot dead in U.S. visa riot in Sierra Leone.

text.p: One man was shot dead and 20 injured in U.S. visa riots in Sierra Leone during which police opened fire to disperse a mob threatening to attack the central post office, doctors said on Thursday.

The dead man was shot in the chest as hundreds of angry youths and young men rioted in the capital Freetown on Wednesday, accusing the post office of dumping applications for an annual U.S. visa lottery in the sea, they added.

"The dead man, Patrick Fortune, was shot in the chest and the bullets pierced his lungs," one doctor at the Connaught Hospital in Freetown told Reuters. "More than 10 other victims were shot in the leg and arm and other parts of the body."
President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who took office last March after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule and has signed a peace deal with rebels, criticised the police for opening fire.
"Shooting," he told state radio late on Wednesday, "is against the spirit of peace and reconciliation the nation is seeking."
Police, who also used tear gas to disperse the protesters, said they had fired in the air after the mob trying to storm the central post office started hurling stones at them.
Post office officials denied destroying the visa applications, which were part of an annual lottery organised by the United States to give a limited number of would-be migrants a work permit.
Protesters said they saw visa forms being put in the sea and had fished out some with Sierra Leone stamps on the envelopes.
Tejan Kabbah, who called on police to investigate the cause of the riots, warned the public "against plunging the country into chaos again after six years of war".
A tense calm returned to the city centre after the shooting but witnesses spokes of running battles elsewhere.
Tejan Kabbah and the rebels, who took up arms in 1991, signed a peace deal in Ivory Coast in December but have yet to reach final agreement on implementation. A ceasefire is in force.
